declarations.docstring: A predicate on a finitely supported natural-valued function, a finite set, and an index.
An index satisfying the predicate lies outside the given finite set.
The coefficient at an index satisfying the predicate is at least one.
Any two indices satisfying the predicate for the same function and finite set are equal.
Adding and then subtracting the same unit singleton leaves a natural-valued finitely supported function unchanged.
The underlying set obtained by adjoining a fresh element to a fixed-cardinality subset is its set insertion.
The degree-zero exterior-power basis evaluates at a zero-cardinality subset as the inverse zero-degree equivalence applied to one.
For an inserted element smaller than every member, the displayed index of each original member increases by one.
An element inserted below every member has displayed index zero in the enlarged finite set.
The displayed index of the minimum element of a nonempty finite set is zero.
Adjoin an absent element to a subset of fixed finite cardinality, producing a subset whose cardinality is one larger.
The index predicate for a natural-valued finitely supported function and finite set is decidable.
The scalar actions of the base ring and its symmetric algebra on the displayed coefficient module form a scalar tower.
The displayed degree-zero projection composed with the displayed coefficient inclusion fixes every coefficient.
The basis-indexed term of the displayed degree-lowering construction.
At degree zero, the displayed differential-homotopy composite plus the coefficient projection-inclusion composite is the identity linear map.
In every successor degree, the two displayed differential-homotopy composites sum to the identity linear map.
The degree-zero homotopy identity holds after evaluation at an arbitrary element.
The degree-zero homotopy identity holds on an element of the displayed basis family.
The successor-degree homotopy identity holds after evaluation at an arbitrary element.
The successor-degree homotopy identity holds on an element of the displayed basis family.
The displayed differential applied to a basis-family element is the sum of its indexwise terms over the underlying finite subset.
A linear map from the displayed symmetric-algebra coefficient module to the degree-zero module.
The coefficient-to-degree-zero map sends a coefficient to the tensor of its symmetric-algebra image with the degree-zero unit.
A basis-dependent linear map from each displayed degree to its successor degree.
The basis-pair formula producing an element in the successor degree.
The basis-pair formula vanishes when no index satisfies the displayed predicate.
When an index satisfies the displayed predicate, the basis-pair formula equals the negation of the displayed successor-degree basis-family value.
The contracting-homotopy map on a displayed basis-family element agrees with the basis-pair formula.
An index belongs to the support after adding a unit singleton exactly when it is the singleton index or belonged to the original support.
If a coefficient is at least one, subtracting and then adding its unit singleton recovers the finitely supported function.
Under positivity at the subtracted index, adding one singleton commutes with subtracting another singleton.
The symmetric-algebra basis sends the zero finitely supported exponent to one.
